geometry_edits.rationale: Swap the generic inflate swell for a taper to preserve one dominant mass while improving sectional hierarchy.
Use a vertical taper so the upper volume becomes calmer and the base remains anchored.
Preserve the original base footprint as a clean anchor.
Narrow the top modestly to strengthen hierarchy without over-sculpting the mass.
Keep the surface continuity smooth and avoid fragmenting the silhouette.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the pure swell with a more legible massing operation that can create a clearer public threshold and stronger program hierarchy.
Add a courtyard macro to carve a usable public void without fragmenting the compact dominant mass.
Keep the void substantial enough to read as inhabitable public space rather than a decorative notch.
Open the courtyard toward the verified access side so the ground response aligns with the public frontage.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent compact mass in all four views, so it avoids outright fragmentation and view-to-view collision, but it is still too object-like for the neighborhood-living brief. The dominant gesture is readable as one compact profiled prism with mild tapering/stepping, yet the open-space figure is essentially absent: there is no meaningful courtyard, undercut, notch, terrace, or entry seam that responds to the verified frontage/access edge. The blue access edge is met by a sealed side rather than a public threshold, which is the main semantic failure. The silhouette is acceptable as a generic early mass, but not yet a convincing neighborhood building because the ground relation and program hierarchy are underdeveloped. The form resonates only loosely with the references: it shares compact low-rise massing, but not their court/public-void logic or articulated threshold. Program fit therefore fails the hard pass because the visible mass does not plausibly support an active ground edge and one clear public void/terrace required by the brief.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion-like and refined; candidate lacks the carved public center and connective hierarchy.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise community massing with a strong central void and upper-level bridge/connector can make a neighborhood building read as one public ensemble.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is much larger and more distributed; candidate is too compact and sealed to transfer the spatial sequence directly.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like low-rise aggregation can support neighborhood program when a central court organizes the mass and the edges step around it.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate has almost no legible threshold relation to the access edge and reads more as a closed object.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A clear cutout or recess at ground level can produce an active public threshold even in a simple rectangular mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is elongated and porous; candidate is compact and not sufficiently open or sectional.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A folded, horizontally spread volume with a central atrium/courtyard can give neighborhood scale without becoming fragmented.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is multi-part and topographically articulated; candidate has a single sealed mass with only mild stepping.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, connected wings around a usable court can make upper hierarchy and public open space work together.

warnings: Access edge appears unresolved: the mass does not open toward the verified road frontage.

The form is coherent but generic, with limited neighborhood-program specificity.
